events.excerpt: This release contains bugfixes and improvements to the stacks-node and stacks-signer binaries, ensuring more consistent block production. This release is compatible with chainstate directories from 4.0.x. This release is recommended for all Stacks node and signer operators. This release includes the following changes: https://github.com/stacks-network/stacks-core/blob/4.0.7/CHANGELOG.md Fixed Fixed nodes being unable to download a large Nakamoto tenure. A /v3/tenures response could hold up to 16 MiB of blocks, but the receiving node counts the response's chunk framing against the same limit and dropped the connection before the end, so a node that missed blocks in a tenure larger than about 16 MiB could never fetch them. /v3/tenures now leaves room for chunk framing so that nodes can read its responses. events.excerpt: Binance said Thursday it has replaced every token lost in its record $6.3 billion hack. Customers cannot verify it yet, since the proof behind its new reserves snapshot is still pending. That proof is a zero-knowledge proof, a math-based check that lets users confirm the exchange holds at least one coin for every coin it owes. Until it is published, the backing for roughly $132 billion in customer assets rests on Binance’s word. What Did Binance Replace, and Who Paid for It? Hackers drained Binance wallets on October 29. The FBI later blamed TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit. It asked exchanges to block wallets tied to the theft. By November 2, Binance said it had refilled about 98% of the affected assets. The remaining gap sat mostly in thinly traded tokens, which the exchange then bought on the market. Binance has said customers will not bear the loss. It paid from its corporate treasury and insurance funds, according to Bloomberg . It also tapped its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), an emergency reserve usually kept near $1 billion. events.excerpt: A Zcash governance trilogy, part 3 of 3. Or navigating the dark forest without turning on all the lights TL;DR: In a private system we cannot know who holds voting power, how many people sit behind it, or whom they are connected to. The answer is not to abolish the privacy. It is to bound what any vote can decide, so that capturing one voting mechanism cannot confer control over the whole system. Part 1 : An Ode to Rough Consensus . Part 2 : When We Disagree: Making Rough Consensus Work . Part 3 : Governance in a Shielded World. Zcash is building a parallel financial system, outside of but adjacent to the existing one. Its governance, however, remains entirely inside human institutions. That private financial system starts from a different assumption from the one we have become accustomed to elsewhere: privacy is normal. In such a system, private by default should be the ordinary situation, not a special mode for people with something to hide. Traditional finance already runs part of its markets this way. Dark pools let large investors trade without displaying their orders, so that others cannot trade against them. Dark does not mean lawless. events.excerpt: For most people, just getting any old microcontroller or system on chip (SoC) from our favorite – or cheapest – vendor is more than good enough. But if you’re really into high assurance computing where every transistor has to be accounted for, you got a bit of a problem. This is basically why [Andrew “Bunnie” Huang] pitched in and had the Baochip-1x produced . This SoC’s design is based heavily on the FPGA-based CPU in the Precursor device , which itself is claimed to be a fully verifiable communicator design. Since it does have an MMU, you can run any software on it that supports the RV32IMAC RISC-V instruction set, with a Coder’s Guide available for those who might feel interested in this SoC, along with the SystemVerilog and Verilog-based sources . In addition to the DIY assembly process, you can even get a physical hardware version, including the ‘Dabao’ evaluation board with a very Raspberry Pi Pico-shaped form factor. Inside this SoC is a single-core, 350 MHz VexRISC-V core, 4 MB resistive RAM (RRAM) and 2 MB of SRAM, along with a whole heap of security-related features.
events.headline: Baochip-1x: A Mostly-Open, 22nm SoC for High Assurance Applications

events.excerpt: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen . These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen's purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google's ecosystem use. With Google's recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company's products. Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it's 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces "fabricated claims" by more than 5x, according to Google's analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash's score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. Read full article
events.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Hydrogen, finally replacing 3.8 Flash

In a Thursday announcement, the exchange wrote that it “has completed coverage of assets impacted in the security incident” and published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot. It repeated the same message on X. That wording matters. Coverage means Binance has replaced the affected tokens from its own books, not that it has recovered the stolen coins from the attackers. Binance has also committed to replenishing SAFU to about $1 billion after that partial draw, a step it said would keep the fund fully resourced as an emergency user-protection reserve. events.excerpt: CHICAGO—Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday, rallying against what they see as Google’s bid to entrench its AI models in schools, turn kids of all ages into Gemini guinea pigs, and hook them on AI. The backlash follows a Google statement last week, confirming that there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. While Google claimed it was giving schools “more choice, not less”—by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default—it would not provide an option that allowed Search without AI. For students, the only way to avoid interacting with AI was to remember to add “-ai” to every query, parents worried. In Chicago, many families showed up to protest Google, despite cold, rainy weather. Waving signs, dozens of protesters marched up to Google’s downtown office as workers seemed to be leaving for the day, shouting chants like “Hey Google, nice try, we don’t want your Gemini” and “Hey, Google, leave our kids alone!” Read full article Comments
events.headline: Google faces calls for AI moratoriums in schools after Gemini pilot backlash

Yet Alex Karp, head honcho of Palantir, seems set to raise the bar with a conspicuous display of political flexibility following the Democratic wave in the US midterms. In December 2024, Karp gave $1 million to the pro-Trump super PAC MAGA Inc . But it does not take cutting-edge AI and data analytics – in which Palantir claims to have unique power – for Karp to understand on which side his bread is buttered. The man with the distinctive verbal diarrhea is now stressing his progressive credentials – and those of Palantir's products. The CEO told Politico that he is now open to voting for the Democrats come 2028. "I've been a Democrat my whole life. I grew up in a far-left environment. I know more about being a progressive than almost anybody on the planet, and I absolutely believe Palantir – all of our products are essentially progressive," Karp reportedly said. Karp's explanation for his political generosity was an apparent desire for balance. "My giving is equal, Democrat, Republican," Karp told the publication. events.excerpt: New York’s Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) has issued new rules that make licensed crypto firms responsible for the influencers they hire for ads and for their impostors too. Crypto firms have until May 10, 2027, to comply with its new rules. What does the new NYDFS guidance require from crypto firms? Licensed virtual currency entities, known as VCEs, now have to operate under the new rules issued by the New York State Department of Financial Services (NYDFS). Acting Superintendent Kaitlin Asrow laid out the rules. First, a firm must be able to prove any claim it makes in an ad. Second, every ad must make clear which licensed company is behind it. Lastly, firms must have real internal processes for how marketing is built, reviewed, and approved. Since the 2015 rulebook took effect, NYDFS has required licensees to include a “licensed by NYDFS” statement in their ads. That statement tells customers that a regulator oversees the firm. The new guidance makes clear that a state license does not mean that the state is endorsing the tokens, trades, or returns it offers. Firms are also warned not to suggest otherwise in their ads. Firms are also now required to check the background of outside partners they work with and watch for people misusing their brand. Policies must be rev
events.headline: NYDFS makes licensed crypto firms answer for their promoters and impostors

events.excerpt: We caught the first trailer for the upcoming Netflix animated film Ray Gunn in September and were charmed by director Brad Bird's blend of a Jetsons-like future with classic 1930s noir detective thrillers. Bird has described it as a mashup of The Maltese Falcon and Buck Rogers , and the latest trailer definitely gives off that energy. As previously reported , Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins. He's been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987’s Batteries Not Included with Bird—“stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,” the director said earlier this year. The film’s inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s’ “ Planet Claire ” (a personal favorite that also provides the soundtrack to the new trailer) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini’s theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn . Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a play on " raygun ," of course).
events.headline: Netflix releases new trailer for Ray Gunn

events.excerpt: This Node and Miner patch release is recommended for all node operators and storage providers. It moves the FVM to wasmtime 48 LTS for performance and security improvements, fixes CreateBackup path containment, and makes Ethereum JSON-RPC quantity validation stricter. Review the upgrade warning before upgrading. ✨ Notable Changes ⚠️ Upgrade warning: Ethereum JSON-RPC rejects negative, unprefixed, leading-zero and oversized (>256-bit) big integers. Use canonical 0x encoding ( 0x0 for zero). The Go helper api.NewErrNegativeGasPrice is removed. ( #13938 ) The FVM now runs on wasmtime 48 LTS for every network version, via ref-fvm v4.9.0 . Security: wasmtime 48 is a long-term-support release that gets security fixes until ~August 2028. Performance: on a mainnet node over 24 hours, median execution time per unit of gas fell about 18% for messages and 11% overall, with no regressions seen on mainnet or calibnet ( measurements ). ( #14023 ) 📝 All Changes Node: Changes since v1.39.0 Miner: Changes since miner/v1.39.0 All PRs (9) Fixes fix(api): reject CreateBackup paths outside LOTUS_BACKUP_BASE_PATH ( #14020 ) fix(eth)!: reject non-canonical and oversized JSON quantities ( #13938 ) Chores and other build: update Lotus Node and Miner version to v1.39.1-dev in master ( #14010 ) chore(deps)
events.headline: v1.39.1

events.excerpt: Crypto wallet firm Trezor has cut its reseller network by 80% following the discovery of more spy implants in devices sold by Malaysian vendor CryptoBilis. Trezor’s latest update on the spyware incident revealed it has implemented stricter rules for vendors in order to protect its supply chain. However, only 20% of vendors were able to abide by the new rules that focus on “how devices are sourced, stored and who has access to them.” Trezor stressed, however, that the dropped resellers “were trustworthy and posed no immediate threat.” Trezor says its new update renders spy implants useless Trezor also claims to have released an update on November 11 that stops the implants recording data and renders them “useless.” A spokesperson for the company told Protos, “The implant listens to the communication between the MCU and the display and triggers the capture when it sees a specific sequence.” In order to stop the sequence trigger, which is a wallet’s seed phrase, Trezor claims it “changed the order of the commands sent to the display” and that it can do this “without any effect on the displayed screen.” Trezor shared the interior of one of the tampered CryptoBilis-sourced wallets. Read more: Trezor reveals Malaysian reseller sold wallet with spyware Despite this, Trezor warned Crypto
events.headline: Trezor cuts reseller network by 80% after finding more spy implants

events.excerpt: During an hour-long event on Thursday, Abel Avellan, the founder and chief executive of the telecommunications company AST SpaceMobile, laid out his vision for developing a large rocket to launch his Bluebird satellites into orbit. Avellan emphasized, over and over again, that AST plans to build a "simple" rocket. He paraphrased SpaceX founder Elon Musk several times, saying, "the best part is no part." Avellan emphasized that AST has already procured engines for its proposed Blacklift rocket, asserting that engine development accounts for 80 percent of a typical rocket's development cycle. "Of course rocket engineers are going to get mad with me, but you can simplify it as a big tank feeding engines," he said of the rocket. "So big tanks—we know how to do them. We know how to do them. We know how to do them in composite." Read full article Comments

events.excerpt: Release Notes Node version 11.2.1 is a pre-release version of cardano-node that is not yet recommended for use on mainnet. It is a maintenance release on top of 11.2.0 . It updates to ouroboros-consensus 5.4, cardano-api 11.12 and cardano-cli 11.7, which together reduce the node's memory use around ledger snapshots, and it raises the protocol version the node advertises in block headers to 11.3. For the full set of 11.2 changes (the new cardano-config configuration format, gRPC over HTTP/2, the removal of node-to-client versions below NodeToClientV_23 , and more), see the 11.2.0 release notes . Highlights: Lower memory use. Writing a ledger snapshot no longer temporarily grows live memory by about the snapshot's size. The ChainDB also no longer keeps the genesis ledger state alive, which saves several hundred MiB on networks with a large genesis UTxO or delegation set. Faster snapshots while syncing. Until the node has first caught up, ledger snapshots are written as soon as they are requested. The randomised snapshot delay applies only after that. LSM is supported for block production. events.excerpt: For 11 years, a Massachusetts man had an alarming array of health problems, most notably that his heart kept failing. He landed in the hospital over and over again, needed life support at one point, spent years going to specialists, and underwent a barrage of tests along the way. But through it all, he never revealed a key detail behind his ailments: He was taking powerful, illicit synthetic testosterone derivatives (aka anabolic-androgenic steroids, or AAS). One of the drugs he took was approved only for use in animals; it's primarily used to beef up cows. Left in the dark, his doctors had to puzzle this out on their own. In a case report in this week's issue of the New England Journal of Medicine, they explain how they did it. They also offer a warning: These cases will only become more common, and clinicians need to know what they look like. Read full article Comments
events.headline: Man's secret use of synthetic testosterone for cows nearly destroyed his heart
